name: Crypto trend (BTC and ETH above 100-day average, long only)
sources: Liu, Y. and Tsyvinski, A., "Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency", Review of Financial Studies 34(6), 2021, 2689-2727 (NBER working paper w24877). CHECKED against the actual paper text on 2026-09-23 (WP8.2-style, by hand): real paper, confirmed. Confirmed 'documented only IN SPIRIT' is accurate, not a stretch: the paper documents time-series momentum as a general return-predictability factor via return-quintile sorts (Tables 14/15/17), with no mention anywhere of a moving-average or a 100-day rule specifically -- 'moving average' appears exactly once in the whole paper, unrelated (a macro control variable's own definition, not a trading rule). The specific 100-day-SMA rule is genuinely this entry's own construction, not the paper's.

Reference implementation: weightsim_rules::ladder rule id "crypto_trend_100d" (S3), the compiled rule replication::registry::certified_key_bars resolves against the embedded, SHA-256-pinned replication_ladder_crypto_evidence answer key (Amendment 13, crypto_evidence_v1, PR #213).
rule_text: Universe: BTC/USD and ETH/USD (daily closes). Each day, for each coin: if its close is above the simple average of its last 100 daily closes, INCLUDING today's close, hold that coin long at 50% of the sleeve's equity; otherwise hold cash in its place. Rebalance daily at the close. A position decided at the close of day t earns returns from the next trading day's close-to-close return onward; a decision uses only data available at the close of the decision day. Long only, no leverage: maximum gross exposure is 100% of sleeve equity (2 x 50%).
reference_implementation: weightsim_rules::ladder rule id "crypto_trend_100d" (S3), the compiled rule replication::registry::certified_key_bars resolves against the embedded, SHA-256-pinned replication_ladder_crypto_evidence answer key.

notes: min_history_years is the history needed to compute the FIRST signal only (100 daily closes); a meaningful backtest needs far more.

Drafted from RuleTemplate::CryptoTrend100d (library_curation::draft) -- structural fields (requirements, rebalance, parameters, rule_text) are template-fixed, matched here exactly to avoid RULE_DRIFT against the compiled rule.

The published rule rebalances daily to fixed 50/50 weights. The platform runs each coin as an independent sub-account, so weights drift: an approximation of the rule, not a block (cross_asset_rebalance = preferred).

rebalance.detail: Daily at the close of the (UTC) daily bar. Crypto trades every day, so no month-end or holiday handling is needed.

expected_ranges.source: No band, deliberately. Council rulings R22/R23 (COUNCIL_DATA_GATE_2026_09_26.md) and Amendment 13 section 7 (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder_crypto_evidence/AMENDMENT_13.md): expected ranges come from the certified window only, and with an estimated SE of about 0.49 on a single ~6.5-year window (one crypto cycle, not several independent ones), the band stays withdrawn until net-of-cost AND live-realistic (R10) numbers exist -- a policy choice, not a measured kill (the measured net Sharpe's own 95% CI, 1.148 +/- ~0.96, does not include zero).
expected_ranges.note: Window-specific reference only, NOT an expectation for other windows. Certified replication (Amendment 13, crypto_evidence_v1, 2020-03-16 to 2026-10-03, 6.549 years): gross Sharpe 1.185919, CAGR 54.6399%, vol 45.5044%, max drawdown -51.1439%; net (certification_flat_10bps_per_side) Sharpe 1.148372, CAGR 52.0604%, vol 45.5415%, max drawdown -52.5528%. 50/50 BTC/ETH buy-and-hold over the same window (measured 2026-10-09 directly from the pinned primary CSVs, massive_btcusd_daily.csv / massive_ethusd_daily.csv, no rebalancing -- matching the platform's own independent-sub-account convention): final equity 20.44x, max drawdown -77.60%. The 2016-2020 figures from the legacy, non-evidence fixture (Sharpe 2.10, CAGR 218%) must not appear on any customer-facing surface (R23(e)) and are not repeated here.

known_deviations: The platform runs each coin as an independent sub-account, so weights drift from the published fixed 50/50 rather than truly rebalancing daily (cross_asset_rebalance: preferred, not a hard block).

Evidence window is one crypto cycle (2020 COVID crash, 2021 top, 2022 decline, 2023-2026 recovery) -- a single regime sequence, not several independent cycles; this is exactly why no performance band is published (see expected_ranges[0].source).

C4 venue check (data_quality_certificate.json): Kraken-vs-primary comparison only covers the last 720 days of the window (Kraken's own public history limit); no exception above 150bp was found in that sub-window, but the earlier ~5.5 years have no independent third-source venue check, only the Bitstamp arbiter.
failure_regimes: Bull-market dependence: the rule's edge over buy-and-hold can be small in a strong uptrend (certified net Sharpe 1.148 vs a 50/50 buy-and-hold max drawdown of -77.6% that the rule's own -52.55% net drawdown improves on, but both windows share the same underlying bull market).
Deep drawdowns: crypto volatility (45.5% annualised in the certified window) can far exceed a typical drawdown ladder without scaling down.

Sideways or choppy markets where prices repeatedly cross the 100-day average (whipsaw). GENERAL property of moving-average trend rules; 198 signal flips over 6.549 years in the certified window is the measured turnover, not a claim about future whipsaw frequency.

cost_profile.note: Turnover as a multiple of sleeve equity is NOT recorded in the local files. The certified replication (key_metrics.json) counted 198 asset-level signal flips over 6.548939 years (2393 observations at 365.4027 per year), about 30.2 per year across the two coins. The certified net result above uses the certification_flat_10bps_per_side accounting cost (turnover_sum_x_equity 110.4162, cost_sum_x_equity 0.110416), not a measured spread/impact model for any live venue.

verification_note: Rule text, parameters, requirements and rebalance are copied verbatim from library_curation::draft::RuleTemplate::CryptoTrend100d (the platform's own compiled-rule-template menu) rather than retyped, to guarantee zero drift against the compiled weightsim-rules S3 adapter. Backtest window and all performance numbers come from Amendment 13's real, pre-registered evidence fixture (program/tests/fixtures/replication_ladder_crypto_evidence/, PR #213, merged 2026-10-04): real data pulled by the owner (Massive primary, Bitstamp arbiter, Kraken venue check) per the pre-registered window rule (section 3) and data-quality certificate (section 4), verdict PASS on all of C1/C2/C3/C5 (data_quality_certificate.json), T4 mutation-power check passed (all 5 S3 mutants caught by at least one tier, mutant_replays.json: all_mutants_caught=true, mutants_blocking_certification=[]). This fixture was built and fully certified on 2026-10-04 but its own final step -- drafting this entry -- was never done until now (2026-10-09); nothing in program/src referenced the fixture before this file. The one number NOT already sitting in the fixture, the 50/50 BTC/ETH buy-and-hold drawdown over the certified window, was measured today directly from the fixture's own pinned primary CSVs (massive_btcusd_daily.csv / massive_ethusd_daily.csv) rather than invented: -77.60% (no cross-coin rebalancing, matching the platform's own independent-sub-account convention; a daily-rebalanced 50/50 variant gives a close -76.29%, consistent with the council record's unweighted BTC-alone figure of -76.7%). Per Amendment 13 section 7 and council rulings R22/R23, no performance band is published despite the certification passing representativeness (9.8): the council's own stated reason is statistical power (SE ~0.49 on one ~6.5-year window spanning a single crypto cycle), a deliberate policy choice, not a failed check -- see expected_ranges[0].source for the exact reasoning and the measured net Sharpe's own confidence interval. The Liu & Tsyvinski (2021) citation was checked against the actual paper text on 2026-09-23 (reused verbatim from this entry's own pre-existing test fixture, program/data/strategy_library/test_fixtures/crypto_trend_100d.json) and honestly disclosed as covering cryptocurrency return predictability generally, not this specific 100-day-SMA rule -- citation_claims is deliberately left empty rather than attaching an invented quote/number pairing that would misrepresent the paper's actual content. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE of the withheld performance band: replication::admission::admission_for's 9.7_evidence_strength check requires a PerformanceBand range with a real low bound, which this entry does not have -- this entry is therefore served on GET /api/library (real, visible data) but is Held, not Admitted, and proposals.rs rejects any mandate's attempt to actually propose it with that exact reason until a performance band is published.
retirement_rule: Flag to the inbox for a human decision (the agent may not remove it on its own) when any of: (a) the monthly fidelity check finds signal agreement with the compiled reference implementation below 0.98; (b) the sleeve's own replayed drawdown reaches the mandate's first drawdown rung; (c) realised net results over a full evaluation window fall outside a performance band once one is published; (d) a later decay_check replication run against this same rule_hash fails. The window length and any numeric tolerance for (c) must be set by the owner before go-live; none is assumed here.
